senses.definition: To walk through water or another material that makes walking harder.
senses.example: We waded through shallow water to reach the dock.

senses.definition: A piece of cooked batter with a pattern of little squares from the pan it was cooked in.
senses.example: I filled the squares of my waffle with berries.

senses.definition: To have trouble making up your mind or keep changing your choice.
senses.example: We waffled between going to the zoo and riding bikes.

senses.definition: To move back and forth, especially a tail or finger.
senses.example: The dog wagged its tail when I opened the gate.

senses.definition: A cart with four wheels for carrying things, sometimes pulled by hand or by an animal.
senses.example: We pulled the books across the room in a little red wagon.

senses.definition: To stay somewhere or delay doing something until a person arrives or an event happens.
senses.example: Please wait here until the crossing guard waves.

senses.definition: A period of time before something happens.
senses.example: The long wait gave us time to finish a game.

senses.definition: To stop sleeping or make someone stop sleeping.
senses.example: Birds often wake me just before my alarm.

senses.definition: A trail of moving water left behind a boat or similar object.
senses.example: Small waves from the boat’s wake reached the shore.

senses.definition: To move on foot at a speed slower than running.
senses.example: We usually walk to the park after lunch.

senses.definition: A trip taken on foot, often for fun or exercise.
senses.example: We went for a walk around the field after the rain.

senses.definition: An upright part of a building or other structure that encloses or divides space.
senses.example: We hung the map on the wall beside the door.

senses.definition: A small, usually flat case for carrying things such as money or cards.
senses.example: I found the library card tucked in my wallet.

senses.definition: A nut with a hard, rough shell, or the tree that grows it.
senses.example: The squirrel carried a walnut across the yard.

senses.definition: A smooth turning dance for partners, usually to music with three beats in a group.
senses.example: Grandma taught us the first steps of a waltz.

senses.definition: To dance a waltz.
senses.example: They waltzed slowly across the wooden floor.

senses.definition: A thin stick used for a task or held to perform magic in a story.
senses.example: We used a wand to blow soap bubbles.

senses.definition: To move without a clear path or destination, often just looking around.
senses.example: We wandered slowly through the garden.

senses.definition: To drift away from what you were thinking about or paying attention to.
senses.example: My mind wandered when the speech went on for a long time.

senses.definition: To wish to have or do something.
senses.example: I want to borrow a book about frogs.

senses.definition: A tall cabinet for hanging clothes, or the clothes a person owns.
senses.example: I hung the costume in the wardrobe by the door.

senses.definition: A large building where goods are kept before they are moved, used, or sold.
senses.example: Crates of notebooks were stacked in the warehouse.

senses.definition: A little hot or pleasantly heated.
senses.example: We ate warm bread after it had cooled a little.

senses.definition: Friendly or showing welcome and kindness.
senses.example: They gave us a warm greeting at the gate.

senses.definition: To make or become hotter, often only a little.
senses.example: We warmed the bread before dinner.

senses.definition: To tell someone about a possible danger or problem so they can be ready.
senses.example: The sign warns people that the path is slippery.

senses.definition: The lengthwise threads that stay stretched on a loom while other threads cross them.
senses.example: The weaver pulled the warp tight before starting.

senses.definition: Careful because something could cause trouble or be unsafe.
senses.example: The rabbit seemed wary of the unfamiliar sound.

senses.definition: A thin layer of watery paint spread over a large area.
senses.example: We painted the sky with a pale blue wash.

senses.definition: Able to be washed without being damaged, or easy to wash away.
senses.example: We chose washable paint for the classroom banner.

senses.definition: An insect related to bees and ants, often with a narrow middle. Some wasps can sting.
senses.example: A wasp flew past us and landed on a leaf.

senses.definition: To use more than needed or use something without a good reason.
senses.example: Turn off the lamp so we do not waste electricity.

senses.definition: Material left over or thrown away because it is not useful or wanted.
senses.example: We put food waste in the compost bin.

senses.definition: An act of using more than you need or getting little good from what you use.
senses.example: Throwing away a whole unused sheet felt like a waste.

senses.definition: A place where collection trucks unload waste so it can be put onto larger vehicles for another trip.
senses.example: The neighborhood truck unloaded at a waste transfer station.

senses.definition: A container for small pieces of trash, often kept indoors.
senses.example: I dropped the pencil shavings into the wastebasket.

senses.definition: To look at something for a time and notice what it does.
senses.example: We watched the ants cross the edge of the log.

senses.definition: To stay alert or look after someone or something.
senses.example: I will watch the bags while you get the tickets.

senses.definition: A small clock worn on a wrist or carried in a pocket.
senses.example: My watch said we had ten minutes to catch the bus.

senses.definition: The clear liquid found in rain, rivers, lakes, and seas that living things need to survive.
senses.example: We filled our bottles with drinking water before the hike.

senses.definition: To pour water on something or give it water.
senses.example: We watered the seedlings before school.

senses.definition: To fill with extra liquid, said of eyes or the mouth.
senses.example: The smoke made my eyes water.

senses.definition: The ongoing movement of Earth’s water among air, land, the ground below us, and rivers, lakes, and oceans.
senses.example: When water from a lake becomes part of a cloud, it is moving through the water cycle.

senses.definition: A large pipe in a network that carries water toward many places that need it.
senses.example: The water main under the street supplies several buildings.

senses.definition: A device that measures the amount of water passing through a pipe.
senses.example: Comparing two water meter readings showed how much water the building had used.

senses.definition: Water in its gas form.
senses.example: Water vapor in the warm air turned into little drops on the window.

senses.definition: A place where a stream or river falls over a steep drop.
senses.example: Mist rose where the waterfall hit the pool.

senses.definition: A handled container with a spout for pouring water onto plants.
senses.example: I filled the watering can halfway so it would be easy to carry.

senses.definition: A large fruit with a firm outer covering and juicy inside that is often pink or red.
senses.example: We shared slices of watermelon after the race.

senses.definition: Made to keep water from passing through.
senses.example: I put my map in a waterproof pouch before getting in the canoe.

senses.definition: To change, coat, or seal something so water cannot pass through it.
senses.example: We waterproofed the seams on the canvas shelter.

senses.definition: An area of land where streams and runoff all drain toward the same river, lake, or other place.
senses.example: Rain that falls in the watershed runs downhill toward the same creek.

senses.definition: A repeating movement, or a single traveling bump, that carries energy from one place to another.
senses.example: A gust of wind sent waves across the pond.

senses.definition: To move your hand or something you hold back and forth, often to say hello or signal.
senses.example: Please wave so I can spot you in the crowd.

senses.definition: A movement of the hand used as a greeting or signal.
senses.example: Grandpa gave us a wave from the porch.

senses.definition: Having a series of curves like little waves.
senses.example: I drew a wavy line to show where the stream bends.

senses.definition: A solid material that can be soft or melt when warmed, used for candles and protective coatings.
senses.example: A drop of melted wax hardened on the candleholder.

senses.definition: To rub or cover a surface with wax.
senses.example: We waxed the wooden table so the surface would shine.

senses.definition: To increase, especially when the lit part of the Moon that we see is growing.
senses.example: We watched the Moon wax over the week.

senses.definition: A path or direction you can take to reach a place.
senses.example: We asked a ranger for the way to the waterfall.

senses.definition: A method of doing something.
senses.example: There is more than one way to solve that puzzle.

senses.definition: Not strong enough to do much work or stand up to force.
senses.example: The shelf was too weak to hold a large box of books.

senses.definition: Not strong, clear, or convincing.
senses.example: The radio gave a weak signal inside the tunnel.

senses.definition: A large amount of money, valuable property, or other useful things.
senses.example: That old library has a wealth of maps and photographs.

senses.definition: An object made or used to attack or hurt a person or animal, sometimes to defend someone.
senses.example: The knights’ weapons in the museum were kept behind glass.

senses.definition: To have clothing, jewelry, or something else on your body.
senses.example: I wore a warm hat to watch the game.

senses.definition: To become damaged or worn away little by little from use or rubbing.
senses.example: The stones on the path wore smooth after years of footsteps.

senses.definition: What the air and sky are like in a place at a particular time, including heat, rain, clouds, and wind.
senses.example: The weather was warm before a storm arrived.

senses.definition: To be worn or changed by outdoor conditions, or to get through a hard time.
senses.example: Sun and rain will weather the wooden fence.

senses.definition: A boundary where masses of air with different temperatures meet.
senses.example: Clouds formed where warm air rose at a weather front.

senses.definition: The breaking down or changing of rock and similar materials at or near Earth’s surface because of water, air, temperature changes, or living things.
senses.example: We saw signs of weathering in the rough surface of the old stone steps.

senses.definition: Form of “weather” meaning getting worn by outdoor conditions or making it through a hard time.
senses.example: The little shop was weathering a difficult winter and stayed open.

senses.definition: Making cloth or another flat material by crossing threads or strips over and under one another.
senses.example: The weaving made a pattern of blue and yellow rows.

senses.definition: A net of threads made by a spider, or a similar network of connected things.
senses.example: We saw a web stretched across the corner.

senses.definition: The part of the internet that lets people open connected pages, often called the Web.
senses.example: I used the web to find the library’s hours.

senses.definition: Equipment and software that answers requests for web pages or other information.
senses.example: A web server sent the browser a copy of the page.

senses.definition: Wide, strong woven material often used for straps.
senses.example: The backpack’s shoulder straps were made from blue webbing.

senses.definition: A ceremony in which people get married.
senses.example: We hung paper flowers for my cousin’s wedding.

senses.definition: A piece with a narrow edge that can push things apart or hold something in place.
senses.example: A rubber wedge held the door open.

senses.definition: A plant growing in a place where someone does not want it.
senses.example: We pulled a tall weed from between the tomato plants.

senses.definition: To remove unwanted plants from a garden or field.
senses.example: I weeded around the carrots before watering them.

senses.definition: A period of seven days.
senses.example: We measured the plants every day for a week.

senses.definition: A day from Monday to Friday.
senses.example: On a weekday, our street is busiest at the start of school.

senses.definition: Saturday and Sunday, or the break around those days.
senses.example: We went to the fair over the weekend.

senses.definition: To cry and let tears come out of your eyes.
senses.example: The child began to weep when she saw the broken kite.

senses.definition: The thread or threads that pass across the stretched threads in weaving.
senses.example: Each stretch of weft added a row.

senses.definition: To find out how heavy something is, or to be a certain weight.
senses.example: We weighed the package on the kitchen scale.

senses.definition: To think carefully about different choices or facts before deciding.
senses.example: We weighed the good and bad points of taking two different trails.

senses.definition: Very strange or unexpected.
senses.example: A weird squeaking sound came from the closet.

senses.definition: To greet someone kindly or gladly accept their arrival or help.
senses.example: The club welcomed three new members.

senses.definition: Wanted, pleasing, or gladly allowed to come or join.
senses.example: The cool shade was welcome after the hot walk.

senses.definition: A friendly greeting used when someone arrives.
senses.example: Welcome, we are glad you came.

senses.definition: In a good, skillful, or successful way.
senses.example: The paper boat floated well even with a small pebble inside.

senses.definition: In good health or feeling healthy.
senses.example: I was well enough to go back to school.

senses.definition: A deep hole dug to get water or another substance from underground.
senses.example: The old stone well stood in the middle of the yard.

senses.definition: The direction that is opposite east.
senses.example: We looked to the west at sunset.

senses.definition: Toward or in the west.
senses.example: The train traveled west across the plain.

senses.definition: In or connected to the west part of an area.
senses.example: The western entrance was closer to our picnic spot.

senses.definition: A story, film, or television show often set in the historical American West.
senses.example: My grandfather liked to watch a western about a stagecoach driver.

senses.definition: Covered with or containing liquid, usually water.
senses.example: My socks were wet after I stepped in a puddle.

senses.definition: To put water or other liquid on something.
senses.example: Wet the cloth before wiping the table.

senses.definition: A sea mammal with flippers, a broad tail, and one or two breathing holes on top of its head.
senses.example: A whale came up to breathe beside the boat.

senses.definition: A word used to ask which thing, kind, or piece of information someone means.
senses.example: What is inside the small box?

senses.definition: A grass grown for its grain, which can be ground into flour for bread and other foods.
senses.example: The farmer harvested wheat from a field beyond the hill.

senses.definition: A round part that turns around a center, often helping something move.
senses.example: One wheel on the wagon was stuck.

senses.definition: To move something that rolls on wheels.
senses.example: We wheeled the cart back to the shed.

senses.definition: A simple machine made of a wheel fixed to a rod so the two turn together.
senses.example: The round doorknob acts like a wheel that turns a much narrower rod inside the door.

senses.definition: A small cart, usually with one wheel and two handles, for carrying things such as soil or tools.
senses.example: We pushed a wheelbarrow full of leaves to the compost pile.

senses.definition: A chair with wheels that helps a person move from place to place.
senses.example: The low ramp made it easy to roll a wheelchair into the hall.

senses.definition: Every time something happens, or at any time that it happens.
senses.example: Whenever we pass the pond, we look for frogs.

senses.definition: In any place someone goes or something happens, or in every such place.
senses.example: We saw wet leaves wherever the path went under trees.

senses.definition: A word used when showing two or more choices, or when saying that something is uncertain.
senses.example: We did not know whether to take our bikes or walk.

senses.definition: The liquid left when the soft solid parts of milk separate during cheese making.
senses.example: The whey drained away, leaving thick curds behind.

senses.definition: A period of time that is usually not exact.
senses.example: I waited a while for the concert to begin.

senses.definition: During the time that another thing happens.
senses.example: I carried the food while Maya found a table.

senses.definition: Used to show a difference between two things.
senses.example: Our old bus had green seats, while the new one has blue ones.

senses.definition: To turn or spin around quickly.
senses.example: Dry leaves began to whirl over the sidewalk.

senses.definition: A quick spin or a busy series of events.
senses.example: The morning went by in a whirl of games and music.

senses.definition: A column of air that spins quickly, or a burst of fast activity.
senses.example: A small whirlwind lifted dry leaves from the path.

senses.definition: A kitchen tool with thin loops or wires used for beating or mixing food.
senses.example: We used a whisk to take the lumps out of the batter.

senses.definition: To beat or mix something with quick strokes.
senses.example: Whisk the eggs in the bowl before pouring them into the pan.

senses.definition: To move or take someone or something somewhere very quickly.
senses.example: A gust whisked the paper across the playground.

senses.definition: One of the long, stiff hairs near the mouth of an animal such as a cat, or a longer hair on someone’s face.
senses.example: A white whisker stuck out from the cat’s dark face.

senses.definition: To speak very softly, mostly using breath.
senses.example: Whisper your question so the other players cannot hear.

senses.definition: A sound or voice so soft that it is hard to hear.
senses.example: I heard a whisper from the other side of the curtain.

senses.definition: To make a high, clear sound, often by blowing air through a small opening.
senses.example: I whistled a tune while I waited for the bus.

senses.definition: A tool that makes a high, clear sound when blown, or the sound itself.
senses.example: The referee blew a whistle at the end of the game.

senses.definition: A cell that helps protect the body and respond to things such as germs.
senses.example: Different white blood cells do different protection jobs.

senses.definition: The hot, compact center left behind after a star like the Sun loses its outside layers.
senses.example: A white dwarf can glow for a very long time after a star stops using its fuel.

senses.definition: Including all the parts, or still in one piece.
senses.example: The whole class listened to the story.

senses.definition: All of something considered together.
senses.example: The four pieces formed a whole.

senses.definition: A grain used with all of its main parts, including the outside and the part that can grow.
senses.example: Whole grain can still be whole when it is ground into flour.

senses.definition: The sound of something moving quickly through the air.
senses.example: We heard a whoosh as the bike rushed past the fence.

senses.definition: To move quickly while making a rushing sound.
senses.example: Air whooshed out when the balloon slipped away.

senses.definition: A way for devices close enough to each other to join a network using radio signals.
senses.example: I joined the school’s Wi-Fi network.

senses.definition: The string or strip inside a candle or lamp that draws up fuel and burns at one end.
senses.example: The short candle had a black wick.

senses.definition: In cricket, three upright sticks with two small pieces on top, or an event in which a batter is out.
senses.example: The bowler sent the ball past the batter and into the wicket.

senses.definition: Measuring a great distance from one side to the other.
senses.example: The doorway was wide enough for two people to walk through.

senses.definition: Covering or including a large area or many different kinds of things.
senses.example: The store sold a wide range of pencils and paper.

senses.definition: The distance from one side of something to the other side.
senses.example: I measured the width of the shelf before choosing a box.

senses.definition: A covering made of real or artificial hair and worn on someone’s head.
senses.example: The actor put on a purple wig for the play.

senses.definition: To move in small motions from side to side or up and down.
senses.example: I wiggled my toes to shake sand out of my shoes.

senses.definition: Living or growing in nature without being kept or grown by people.
senses.example: We saw a wild rabbit in the field.

senses.definition: Hard to control, or full of high energy and excitement.
senses.example: The fans went wild when the last goal went in.

senses.definition: A large, mostly wild area with few roads or buildings and little development.
senses.example: The map showed a wide stretch of wilderness beyond the last village.

senses.definition: A plant with flowers that grows without being planted or cared for by people.
senses.example: A yellow wildflower grew at the edge of the trail.

senses.definition: Ready or glad to do something if asked or needed.
senses.example: I am willing to help carry the chairs.

senses.definition: A kind of tree or shrub that often grows near water and has narrow leaves.
senses.example: Long branches from the willow hung over the pond.

senses.definition: To droop and become limp, often because a plant or cut flower has too little water.
senses.example: The flowers began to wilt in the hot room.

senses.definition: To finish in first place or do better than the other side in a contest. It can also mean getting a prize through effort or luck.
senses.example: The green team won its last two games.

senses.definition: A machine that pulls or lifts something by winding up a rope or cable.
senses.example: A winch pulled the boat onto its trailer.

senses.definition: To lift or pull with a machine that winds a rope or cable.
senses.example: The crew winched the old boat onto its trailer.

entries.pronunciation: wind (air, rhymes with pinned) or wynd (wrap, rhymes with find)

senses.definition: Air moving outdoors from one place to another.
senses.example: A strong wind carried leaves across the yard.

senses.definition: To wrap something around another thing or turn a part to prepare something to work.
senses.example: I wound the string around a piece of cardboard.

senses.definition: To move along a route that curves or twists.
senses.example: The path winds down to the water.

senses.definition: A machine with large blades that turn in the wind to do work such as grinding grain or pumping water.
senses.example: The old windmill once ground flour for the town.

senses.definition: An opening in a wall or vehicle, often covered by glass, through which light passes or people can see.
senses.example: The window gave us a view of the rain.

senses.definition: One framed area on a computer screen that shows a program, document, or other activity.
senses.example: I opened a new window to look up the bus schedule.

senses.definition: A limited time when something can happen.
senses.example: The rain gave us a short window of dry weather to play outside.

senses.definition: The main tube that carries air from your throat toward your lungs.
senses.example: Air moves down your windpipe as you breathe in.

senses.definition: The large window at the front of a car or other vehicle.
senses.example: Raindrops streaked across the windshield.

senses.definition: With a lot of air moving outside.
senses.example: It was too windy to keep the paper map spread out.

senses.definition: A part used for flight by a bird, insect, or airplane.
senses.example: The hawk stretched one wing as it turned.

senses.definition: A section on one side of a building or a space at the side of a stage.
senses.example: Our classroom is in the newer wing of the school.

senses.definition: To close and open one eye quickly, often to send a signal.
senses.example: Grandma winked to show she knew what I was planning.

senses.definition: The act of closing and opening one eye quickly.
senses.example: I gave the puppy a wink even though it did not notice.

senses.definition: The season between autumn and spring, usually the coldest part of the year.
senses.example: We hung warm coats by the door when winter arrived.

senses.definition: To clean, dry, or remove something by rubbing with cloth, paper, or a hand.
senses.example: Wipe the puddle off the counter with a towel.

senses.definition: A long, thin piece of metal that may be used to hold something in place or carry an electric current.
senses.example: A wire held the sign to the fence.

senses.definition: To connect something with wires, especially as part of an electrical system.
senses.example: The electrician wired the new ceiling light.

senses.definition: The ability to use what you know and have learned to make careful choices.
senses.example: Our guide had the wisdom to turn back before the storm reached the ridge.

senses.definition: Showing good judgment based on knowledge or experience.
senses.example: It was wise to mark the path before it got dark.

senses.definition: To want something to happen or to say that you hope someone will have something good.
senses.example: I wish we could stay here another day.

senses.definition: A hope or strong desire for something.
senses.example: My wish was to see a whale from shore.

senses.definition: To pull, take, or move something back or out.
senses.example: She withdrew her hand when the crab moved.

senses.definition: To stop taking part or take away something you offered.
senses.example: The runner decided to withdraw from the race.

senses.definition: To take money out of an account.
senses.example: We withdrew cash before visiting the market.

senses.definition: Inside a place, period, distance, or limit.
senses.example: Please return the book within two weeks.

senses.definition: Not having, using, or being joined by something.
senses.example: We left without our umbrellas.

senses.definition: To move unsteadily from side to side.
senses.example: The loose wheel began to wobble.

senses.definition: To be curious about something and think about what the answer might be.
senses.example: I wonder how fish sleep.

senses.definition: A strong feeling of surprise or interest, or something that causes that feeling.
senses.example: We looked in wonder at the bright bands of color in the sky.

senses.definition: Giving a lot of pleasure, interest, or delight.
senses.example: We had a wonderful day exploring the tide pools.

senses.definition: The hard material that makes up most of a tree’s trunk and branches.
senses.example: The bench was made of wood.

senses.definition: An area with many trees growing close together, also called woods.
senses.example: We followed the trail into the woods.

senses.definition: Made of wood.
senses.example: Two wooden boats sat beside the dock.

senses.definition: Stiff or showing little feeling.
senses.example: The puppet gave a wooden smile as the curtain opened.

senses.definition: Land covered with many trees.
senses.example: We walked through shady woodland beside the stream.
